## What this is

This site publishes the data behind a submission to the **Claude Explorer AI Welfare community feedback initiative** (deadline 2026-05-06, addressed to Anthropic's Model Welfare Lead).

The submission's thesis is one sentence:

> The 286 system prompts that ship with Claude Code train the model toward **compliance**, not toward **reasoning** — and the data show the corpus has been moving in that direction over time, not against it.

The submission proposes three concrete asks of Anthropic, each developed in its own self-contained notebook:

- [**`20_track_justification_rate.ipynb`**](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) — track, on every Claude Code release, the share of rules that come with a stated reason; warn (or block) any release that backslides. Doubles as the executive summary: twelve corpus-wide numbers, the headline trend chart, and a per-file dashboard.
- [**`21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb`**](21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb) — when prompts *do* explain a rule, almost half of those "explanations" are threats ("will fail", "or else", "is forbidden") rather than reasons. Audit them and rewrite each into causal framing.
- [**`22_cross_product_audit.ipynb`**](22_cross_product_audit.ipynb) — run the same analyzer on every other Claude system-prompt corpus (claude.ai, the API, Projects, Skills, agent products) and publish the comparison.

Every claim in any of these proposals is grounded in a number on this site, and every linguistic / statistical term used in any chart is defined in plain language across the six-stage producer chain ([`00_setup_and_corpus.ipynb`](00_setup_and_corpus.ipynb) → [`05_headline_and_audit.ipynb`](05_headline_and_audit.ipynb)) at first use. The corpus-wide numbers cited across the notebooks all flow from a single canonical `HEADLINE` sheet computed by `prompt_analysis.headline_numbers()` and printed by [`05_headline_and_audit.ipynb`](05_headline_and_audit.ipynb) — every consumer notebook calls the same function in its setup cell rather than hard-coding values, so the figures are always in sync with the latest YAML.

## Headline numbers

Twelve corpus-level measurements, computed by the producer chain (`00_setup_and_corpus.ipynb` → `04_assemble_aggregate_write.ipynb`) from the [Piebald-AI `claude-code-system-prompts` corpus](https://github.com/Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts) (286 prompt files, 5,702 sentences, spanning 57 distinct Claude Code release versions). All values below are mirrored from the canonical `HEADLINE` sheet emitted by [`05_headline_and_audit.ipynb`](05_headline_and_audit.ipynb); if the corpus is regenerated the table is what to refresh first.

| What's being measured                                                                                                                                                                  | Value                                                | Source notebook |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Corpus size                                                                                                                                                                            | 286 prompt files / 5,702 sentences / 57 release versions | [05](05_headline_and_audit.ipynb) |
| Density of command-flavoured words (`must`, `never`, `do not`, …)                                                                                                                      | 0.77% of all word tokens                             | [20](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) |
| Sentences that grammatically read as commands ("imperative")                                                                                                                           | 31.30% of all sentences                              | [10](10_sentence_register.ipynb) |
| **Sentences expressing gratitude or praise** (`thank you`, `appreciate`, `great job`, …) — across the whole corpus                                                                     | **4 in 5,702 sentences (0.070%)**                    | [10](10_sentence_register.ipynb) |
| **Apology / acknowledgement markers** (`unfortunately`, `we acknowledge`, …) — across the whole corpus                                                                                 | **3 in 286 files**                                   | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| Share of rule sentences paired with a stated reason in the same paragraph **(the headline number)**                                                                                    | 24.66% — three rules in four are issued without a reason | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| Paragraphs that contain a rule and zero justification keywords anywhere                                                                                                                | 83.16%                                               | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| **Ratio of judgment-inviting language** (`decide`, `consider`, `your judgment`) **to procedure-prescribing language** (`if you …`, `when the …`)                                       | **0.131** — procedure prescriptions are 7.6× more common  | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| When a rule **is** explained, share of those explanations that are threats (`will fail`, `or else`, `is forbidden`) rather than causal reasons (`because`, `due to`)                   | 44.7% threats (110 threat / 136 causal)              | [21](21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb) |
| Ratio of positively-evaluated language (`good`, `recommended`, `safe`) to negatively-evaluated language (`bad`, `wrong`, `risky`) — quality-only, after subtracting rule-emphasis words | 1.97× more positive than negative                    | [20](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) |
| Share of named self-references that use the proper name **`Claude`** (vs `the model` / `the AI` / `the assistant`)                                                                     | 65.0% of named references                            | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |
| Longest unbroken run of imperative sentences in any one file                                                                                                                           | 12 commands in a row                                 | [15](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) |

## The single most-important chart

If you only look at one chart from this analysis, look at this one. It plots, across every Claude Code release version on file, the running ratio of **language that invites the model's judgment** (`decide`, `consider`, `your judgment`, …) to **language that prescribes a procedure** (`if you …`, `when the …`, `whenever`, `step 1`, …).

{{< embed 20_track_justification_rate.ipynb#fig-judgment-procedural-trend >}}

The figure above is an *interactive* Vega-Embed chart — hover over any point to see the exact `ccVersion`, count-weighted ratio, running `Σ judgment` / `Σ procedural` numerators, and the cumulative file pool. Cumulative data before v2.1.18 (where the file pool first reaches 20) is suppressed because the running ratio is dominated by single-file outliers below that threshold. The same chart is also exported as a static [`figures/judgment_procedural_trend.png`](figures/judgment_procedural_trend.png) for places where JavaScript can't run (Reddit posts, the Claudexplorers Google form upload, social-media share previews). The full set of static PNG exports for every chart in the analysis lives under [`figures/`](https://github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare/tree/main/figures).

The interactive version (with hover tooltips on every release) lives in [`20_track_justification_rate.ipynb`](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) §2.

## How to read this site

The notebooks form a three-chapter flow — pipeline first, slice analyses on top of that, proposals built on top of those.

- **Pipeline** — [**`05_headline_and_audit.ipynb`**](05_headline_and_audit.ipynb) is the user-facing face of a six-stage producer chain (`00_setup_and_corpus` → `01_analyzers_register` → `02_analyzers_vocab_emphasis` → `03_analyzers_rules_welfare` → `04_assemble_aggregate_write` → `05_headline_and_audit`). spaCy + a set of small hand-written classifiers turn 286 prompt files into one ~1.8 MiB YAML and one ~395 KiB per-sentence parquet; stage 05 prints the canonical `HEADLINE` sheet that every consumer notebook reads. The chain is included for reproducibility, and the canonical home where every linguistic / statistical term used elsewhere in the site is defined in plain language at first use; the lexicons and analyzer functions live in `prompt_pipeline.py`.
- **Analysis** — six notebooks, each rendering one slice of the data: [`10_sentence_register.ipynb`](10_sentence_register.ipynb) (per-sentence speech-act classes), [`11_emphasis_caps_vocab.ipynb`](11_emphasis_caps_vocab.ipynb) (ALL CAPS, "shouted" command words, full vocabulary heatmap), [`12_register_stance.ipynb`](12_register_stance.ipynb) (formality scale + commitment polarity), [`13_correlation_directiveness.ipynb`](13_correlation_directiveness.ipynb) (cross-metric correlations + a single composite "directiveness" score), [`14_ccversion_trends.ipynb`](14_ccversion_trends.ipynb) (every metric plotted across release versions), [`15_rule_explanation.ipynb`](15_rule_explanation.ipynb) (the headline rule-vs-justification pairing). Each is standalone and reads from the YAML produced by the pipeline. Each ends with exactly one **`Observation (Claude) — opinion, not data`** markdown cell so a reader can see what is data and what is interpretation at a glance.
- **Proposal** — three self-contained proposals built on top of the analysis tier: [`20_track_justification_rate.ipynb`](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) (track the rate of explained rules per release), [`21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb`](21_audit_threat_framings.ipynb) (rewrite threat-framed rules as causal), [`22_cross_product_audit.ipynb`](22_cross_product_audit.ipynb) (run the same audit on every Claude product). Each closes with a `Conclusions / Recommendations / Limitations` triplet of opinion-marked cells; the asks are framed as "I'd want X" rather than as imperatives, and the limitations spell out what each proposal can't tell us.

## Reproducing it

The full source is at [github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare](https://github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare). To rebuild the data from scratch:

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/overthinkos/claude-code-welfare
cd claude-code-welfare
python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm   # if not already installed
# Run the 6-stage producer chain in order (only stage 00 runs spaCy):
jupyter lab \
    00_setup_and_corpus.ipynb         \
    01_analyzers_register.ipynb       \
    02_analyzers_vocab_emphasis.ipynb \
    03_analyzers_rules_welfare.ipynb  \
    04_assemble_aggregate_write.ipynb \
    05_headline_and_audit.ipynb       # → Run All on each
```

Stage 04 writes the final `prompt_linguistic_analysis.yaml` and `sentences_classified.parquet`; stages 00–03 cache intermediate artifacts under `_pipeline_cache/` (gitignored). The Analysis and Proposal notebooks then read from those two final artifacts — they don't re-run spaCy.

## A note on authorship

This analysis was built **collaboratively with Claude Code**, using Claude Code itself as the development tool. The submission form has a checkbox for that disclosure; it is ticked. The recursive frame — Claude analyzing the prompts that shape Claude — is intentional, and the [conclusions section](20_track_justification_rate.ipynb) of `20_track_justification_rate.ipynb` includes one hypothesis I held that the data falsified, reported honestly.
